name: CLI launcher
targeting_mechanism: installBundledCliLauncher() has no destination override; HOME redirection was used, so the packaged GUI rendered the launcher to $TESTHOME/.local/bin/chirality and the owner's ~/.local/bin/chirality was never written (sha256 unchanged all run).
rendered_pin: app_user_data='/Users/ryan/.chirality-tranchetest-v/userdata'; exported as CHIRALITY_USER_DATA only when unset

clean_env_test.command: env -i HOME=$TESTHOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin $TESTHOME/.local/bin/chirality project status --project chirality-app-dev
clean_env_test.result: returned the registered worktree project against the TEST daemon with no manual CHIRALITY_USER_DATA

also_verified: daemon status -> daemon half ok (pid 94611, isolated socket)

hazard.finding: createDefaultCliDependencies() (runtime/packages/cli/src/cli.ts:462) constructs LaunchAgentManager with NO options — no label, no keepAlive, no environmentVariables. The bundled CLI therefore CANNOT address an isolated label, and worse: `chirality daemon status` from the fully isolated run reported the OWNER's job gui/501/com.chirality.runtime (path ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.chirality.runtime.plist, program in the owner main checkout). A `chirality daemon stop` or `uninstall` from an isolated-userData run would have booted out / deleted the operator's real agent.
consequences: Stage V could NOT use the bundled CLI for install/start/stop as the launch brief assumed; a node driver instantiating LaunchAgentManager with the frontend caller's exact options plus a test label/dir was used instead (evidence/la-driver.mjs).
the label/keepAlive/env plumbing added in A3 is reachable ONLY through the GUI's runtime-control IPC (createDesktopDaemonLifecycle), never through the CLI the app itself installs.

corollary: a rebuilt app's `chirality daemon install` still renders KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit:false} and NO EnvironmentVariables — the corrected root cause #2 is NOT fixed on the CLI path, only on the in-app runtime-panel path.

incidental: the owner plist's launchctl print shows 'exit timeout = 5', which is exactly the 5.083s bootout-to-death latency measured in V5.
